definition: A guide to the balance of automated tests: many fast unit tests, fewer integration and contract tests that use real dependencies, and a few slow end-to-end tests of critical journeys. The inverted shape - mostly slow browser tests - is the ice-cream cone: slow, flaky and poor at locating failures.
example: The shop runs 1,200 unit tests in 40 seconds, 90 integration tests against real SQL in 4 minutes, and 8 end-to-end journeys on the staging slot.

definition: A check a change must pass before it moves forward - build and tests on a pull request, smoke tests after deployment, a canary SLO comparison before full release. Gates must be fast enough not to be bypassed and reliable enough to be believed, so flaky tests are fixed or quarantined quickly.
example: A pull request cannot merge unless unit, integration and contract tests pass and coverage on changed lines does not fall.

definition: A short set of checks run straight after a deployment to confirm the new version is basically alive - health endpoint, sign-in, a critical journey - before it receives real traffic. Run against the staging slot, a failed smoke test stops the release before any user is affected.
example: After deploying to staging, the pipeline checks /health, signs in, adds to basket and completes a test-card checkout.

definition: Four measures of software delivery performance from the DevOps Research and Assessment programme: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate and time to restore service. They pair speed with stability; the best teams improve both together. Use them to improve a team's system, not to rank people.
example: The shop's DORA workbook shows deployments rising from weekly to several a day while change failure rate falls to about one in twenty.

definition: The time from a change being committed to it running in production. Short lead times come from small changes, fast pipelines and few manual hand-offs, and they shorten the feedback loop between writing code and learning how it behaves.
example: Lead time fell from nine days, waiting for the weekly batch release, to under a day with continuous delivery.

definition: The share of deployments to production that cause a failure needing a fix, rollback or hotfix. It measures the stability side of delivery; smaller changes, better tests, canaries and fast rollback all bring it down.
example: Of 60 production deployments this month, three needed a rollback: a change failure rate of 5%.
